verses.text: These are the words of the Preacher, David's son and king in Jerusalem.
“Vapor upon vapor,” says the Preacher. “Vapor upon vapor. It's all vapor.”
What do people really gain from all the hard work they do under the sun?
One generation leaves and another shows up, but the earth stays forever.
The sun comes up, goes down, and hurries back to where it rises.
The wind blows south, then swings north. It keeps circling, going back around on the same routes.
Every river runs into the sea, and still the sea isn't full. The rivers keep flowing back to where they've always gone.
Everything is more exhausting than words can say. The eye never sees enough, and the ear never hears enough.
What's happened before will happen again. What's been done will be done again. There's nothing new under the sun.
Can anyone point to something and say, “Look, this is new”? It was already here ages before us.
We don't remember the people who came before us. The people still to come won't be remembered by those after them either.
I, the Preacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
I put my heart into using wisdom to explore everything people do under the sky. It's a heavy load God has given humanity to carry.
I've seen everything people do under the sun. Look, it's all vapor, like trying to catch the wind.
You can't straighten what's crooked or count what's missing.
I told myself, “I've gained more wisdom than anyone in Jerusalem before me. I've had real experience with wisdom and knowledge.”
I put my heart into knowing wisdom and figuring out madness and foolishness. I saw that this too was like chasing the wind.
The more wisdom you have, the more grief you feel. Gain more knowledge and you gain more sorrow.
